name: Lake Rifflsee Pitztal
kurzbeschreibung: Lake Rifflsee at 2,232 m in the upper Pitztal: Tyrol's largest natural high-alpine lake, famous for scenic raft cruises framed by majestic glacier peaks.
beschreibung:
Overview

The breathtaking Lake Rifflsee is situated in the upper Pitztal Valley in the municipality of St. Leonhard im Pitztal (Imst district) at an altitude of 2,232 metres above sea level. Covering an expansive water surface of roughly 27 hectares with depths reaching 24 metres, it is celebrated as the largest natural high-altitude mountain lake in Austria. Nestled within an alpine amphitheatre of the Kaunergrat range in the Ötztal Alps—overshadowed by the Seekogel (3,358 m) and the glaciated peaks—the lake captivates visitors with its distinctive milky turquoise tint, caused by suspended glacial flour carried down by alpine meltwater.

Route & Requirements

Thanks to the comfortable 6-passenger Rifflseebahn gondola departing from the valley village of Mandarfen, this high-alpine wonder is effortlessly accessible for leisurely walkers and families. From the mountain terminal, a gentle and well-maintained lakeside circular trail loops around the shoreline in about an hour. Educational display panels inform guests about resilient alpine flora and the geological retreat of ancient glaciers. During the peak summer months, the lake hosts Europe's highest raft cruise: aboard a 140-square-metre wooden raft, passengers glide peacefully across the glacial waters while an experienced guide shares local lore. For seasoned mountaineers, the lake serves as a trailhead for renowned high-altitude routes to the Rifflseehütte (2,293 m), the Taschachhütte, or the demanding Cottbuser Höhenweg trail.

Visit & Arrival

Lake Rifflsee is accessible for hikers from mid-June to mid-October, and serves as an integral part of the winter ski area from December to April. Raft tours run multiple times daily between July and September, weather permitting. Round-trip gondola ticket (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €27.00, children approx. €16.00, children under 10 free; raft tour tickets approx. €15.00 extra. Cable car travel is included free of charge with the regional Pitztal Sommercard. Arriving by car: take the Inntalautobahn A12 to the Imst/Pitztal exit, then follow the L16 Pitztal road for approximately 35 kilometres to Mandarfen (spacious free car park at the base). By public transit: take the train to Imst-Pitztal railway station, connecting directly to VVT bus line 4204 to Mandarfen.

Tips

The circular path around the lake is wide and easily passable for rugged all-terrain strollers. Relax on the sun terraces of either the historic Rifflseehütte or the eco-friendly Sunna Alm at the cable car summit, savoring hearty Tyrolean Gröstl. Be sure to carry a windbreaker, as brisk alpine winds frequently sweep across the 2,200-metre plateau even in July.
